shortDescription: Backup & restore of client options (options.txt) incl. all keybinds — manual snapshots via command/GUI plus automatic rotating backups on change.
oneLiner: Keeps named snapshots of your client settings — the whole options.txt or just the keybinds — so you can put your controls back exactly as they were after a modpack update or a misclick wrecks them.
commands: /vpaoptions export <name> — saves the current options under <name> (name validated: [A-Za-z0-9._-]+, must not start with auto_); scope follows full_options_backup; silently overwrites an existing snapshot of the same name
/vpaoptions restore <name> — restores the named snapshot after writing an auto_<stamp>-prerestore safety snapshot; <name> is suggested from the existing snapshots (auto_ ones included)
/vpaoptions delete <name> — deletes the named snapshot (auto_ snapshots included); <name> is suggested
/vpaoptions list — lists all snapshots, manual ones white/alphabetical first, automatic ones gray/newest-first
/vpaoptions gui — opens the snapshot management screen (deferred via mc.tell so the closing chat screen does not override it)
All of them are client commands (RegisterClientCommandsEvent) with NO .requires() permission gate; registration is gated on module.isModuleEnabled() at registration time only

configKeys.effect: Back up / restore the full options.txt (video, sound, chat, keybinds, ...); set to false to limit both backups and restores to keybinds (key_* lines) only. Note: the automatic pre-restore safety snapshot is always taken at full scope regardless of this setting.

Automatically create a rotating backup at game start whenever the current options differ from the newest automatic snapshot. The check runs exactly once per launch (first client tick), not while playing.
How many automatic backups (auto_* snapshots) to keep before the oldest ones are deleted. The auto_<stamp>-prerestore safety snapshots count against this budget too.

notes:
PROVENANCE: every statement below was re-verified in the current working tree against src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/modules/options/{OptionsModule.java, config/OptionsConfig.java, client/OptionsClientEvents.java, client/OptionsBackupManager.java, client/OptionsBackupScreen.java}, standalone/options/OptionsStandalone.java, build.gradle:450 (standaloneModules entry) and :627-660 (moduleJar packaging), VanillaPlusAdditions.java:176, assets/vanillaplusadditions/lang/en_us.json:109-114 + 164-174, README.md:178-179, CHANGELOG.md:922, plus git log/git tag. No behaviour was observed in-game.

STRUCTURE
- Five source files, no mixins, no DeferredRegister of any kind, no keybind registration, no recipes, no loot, no data/ JSONs. OptionsModule sits in the common package and is registered unconditionally (bundle: VanillaPlusAdditions.java:176; standalone: StandaloneModuleBootstrap via OptionsStandalone, @Mod("vpa_options")), but onInitialize() (OptionsModule.java:36-38) is an empty stub with only the comment "Client events are registered via @EventBusSubscriber on OptionsClientEvents". All behaviour hangs off OptionsClientEvents, @EventBusSubscriber(value = Dist.CLIENT, bus = GAME) (line 36); OptionsBackupManager and OptionsBackupScreen are @OnlyIn(Dist.CLIENT). On a dedicated server the module loads and does exactly nothing. No shouldInitialize() and no isEnabledByDefault() override -> default true from Module.java:73-75. `enabled` and `debug_logging` come from AbstractModuleConfig and are deliberately not listed under configKeys.

STORAGE / FILE LAYOUT
- Snapshots are plain options.txt-format UTF-8 text files at config/vanillaplusadditions/options_backups/<name>.txt (FMLPaths.CONFIGDIR, OptionsBackupManager.java:49-51). Automatic ones use the reserved prefix "auto_" (AUTO_PREFIX, line 35).
- Manual names must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ and must NOT start with "auto_" (isValidName, lines 57-60). The Brigadier argument is StringArgumentType.word(), which additionally allows "+" - such a name passes the parser and is then rejected by isValidName with message.vanillaplusadditions.options.invalid_name. The GUI trims whitespace (screen line 107) and caps the EditBox at 64 chars (line 53).
- isValidName is only applied on EXPORT. exists()/delete()/restore() take any name, so auto_ snapshots can be restored and deleted from the command and the GUI just like manual ones (the suggestion provider lists them too).
- writeSnapshot uses plain Files.write (CREATE + TRUNCATE_EXISTING, lines 192-196): exporting onto an existing name silently overwrites it. Neither the command nor the GUI warns or asks.
- listBackups() (lines 67-94) sorts manual entries first and alphabetically, automatic ones after them newest-first, and it swallows IOException by returning List.of() - a broken/unreadable backup directory therefore looks exactly like "no backups", never like an error.

AUTO BACKUP (one-shot, at game start)
- OptionsClientEvents.onClientTick (lines 79-98) runs on the FIRST ClientTickEvent.Post of the session (title screen) and is guarded by the static `autoBackupChecked` flag. There is no in-session watcher: settings changed during play are captured only at the NEXT start.
- `autoBackupChecked = true` is set at line 84, BEFORE the module/config check at lines 86-89. Enabling the module (or auto_backup) mid-session therefore yields no automatic backup until the next restart.
- autoBackupIfChanged (lines 164-180) compares the current scoped options line-by-line with the newest auto snapshot (max lastModified) and writes auto_<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss> only when they differ; pruneAutoBackups(keep) runs right after.

RESTORE SEMANTICS (the subtle part)
- Order inside restore() (lines 110-153): (1) read the snapshot into memory, (2) write the safety snapshot auto_<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>-prerestore, (3) prune, (4) apply.
- The pre-restore snapshot is ALWAYS full scope - readCurrentScoped(true) at line 116 - even with full_options_backup=false.
- Because it carries the auto_ prefix it counts against auto_backup_keep and pruneAutoBackups runs immediately (line 117), so writing it can push out older auto snapshots. Consequence worth documenting: restoring the OLDEST auto snapshot while auto_backup_keep is already reached deletes that very snapshot as part of the restore - the restore itself still succeeds, because the file was read into memory at line 112 before the prune.
- Path choice is driven by the snapshot CONTENT, not only by config: the full path needs `fullOptions && !snapshotKeybindsOnly` (line 123). If every non-blank line of the snapshot starts with "key_", it is applied as keybinds-only even with full_options_backup=true. Full path = overwrite options.txt, mc.options.load(), KeyMapping.resetMapping(), mc.options.save().
- Keybind-only path (lines 131-152) parses `key_<mapping name>:<value>`, iterates the LIVE mc.options.keyMappings and counts a mapping only when the stored value differs from mapping.saveString(). Mapping names present in the snapshot but absent from the current install (mod removed) are simply never looked at - no warning, no contribution to keysApplied.
- CORRECTION of an overstated earlier claim: with full_options_backup=false, the newest auto snapshot right after a restore is the FULL-scope -prerestore file, so the next start's keybind-only comparison can never match and one extra auto_ backup is written. That newly written snapshot is keybind-only and becomes the newest auto snapshot, so the situation settles after exactly ONE extra backup - it does not repeat at every game start. The same one-off extra snapshot appears whenever full_options_backup is toggled.
- UNCHECKED-EXCEPTION GAP: the keybind path calls InputConstants.getKey(value) (line 146). Vanilla's InputConstants.getKey(String) throws IllegalArgumentException("Unknown key name: ...") - or NumberFormatException from Integer.parseInt - for a value it cannot parse (verified in the decompiled vanilla source the build uses, ~/.gradle/caches/.../com/mojang/blaze3d/platform/InputConstants.java:165-183; that file is NOT part of this repository). restore() only declares IOException and both call sites (OptionsClientEvents.java:162, OptionsBackupScreen.java:146) catch only IOException, so a hand-edited or corrupted key_ line escapes as an unchecked exception instead of the friendly message.vanillaplusadditions.options.error. Files written by the mod itself always contain vanilla-valid values, so this needs a manually edited snapshot.
- Lang string restored_full (en_us.json:171) explicitly warns that some settings (language, resource packs) may need a restart.

CONTRADICTS THE README
- README.md:179 says "automatic rotating backups whenever settings change". The code checks exactly ONCE per game launch (see AUTO BACKUP above); there is no change watcher.
- README.md:179 says "an Options-screen button"; onScreenInit (lines 102-116) injects the button into BOTH OptionsScreen and ControlsScreen (top right, bounds screen.width - 66, 6, 60, 20). CHANGELOG.md:922 describes both screens correctly.
- README has no documentation link for this module and there is NO docs/modules/options.md - this module still has no dedicated documentation page (git ls-files confirms: only the six Java files are tracked under any "options" path).

COMMANDS
- Registered via RegisterClientCommandsEvent, gated on module.isModuleEnabled() at REGISTRATION time (lines 53-56): flipping `enabled` at runtime does not make /vpaoptions appear until commands are re-registered (world rejoin / reconnect). The screen-button injection re-checks isModuleEnabled() on every screen init, so the button does react to a mid-session toggle.
- No .requires() permission gate - it is a pure client command and works for any player, including on servers without the mod.
- restore/delete offer the existing snapshot names as suggestions (BACKUP_SUGGESTIONS, lines 42-45), export does not.
- The bare root literal /vpaoptions has no .executes() - it always needs a subcommand.

GUI (OptionsBackupScreen)
- Name EditBox (max 64) + Create, scrollable ObjectSelectionList (manual entries white, auto entries gray, timestamp right-aligned), Restore / Delete / Done. NO confirmation dialog - clicking Restore acts immediately; the auto pre-restore snapshot is the only safety net.
- Status feedback is a single centered gray line (render, line 90); it survives a window resize (init() is re-run on the same instance) but is lost when the screen closes.
- refreshList() re-selects the previously selected entry by name and deactivates Restore/Delete when it is gone - vanilla's AbstractSelectionList.clearEntries() nulls the selection, so there is no stale-selection bug after a delete or a prune.
- /vpaoptions gui defers setScreen via mc.tell(...) (lines 203-209); source comment: the chat screen closes right after command execution and would override a synchronous setScreen.

STANDALONE JAR
- build.gradle:450 registers [ moduleId: 'options', displayName: 'Vanilla Plus: Options' ] with no mixins, no dataGlobs and no moduleDeps. The module jar packs only modules/options/** plus standalone/options/** (build.gradle:640-643); the lang file lives in assets/vanillaplusadditions/** and is packed into vpa_core (build.gradle:617), which every module jar requires - so the GUI/message translations still resolve in the standalone setup.

DEAD / INERT
- debug_logging has NO effect here: nothing in the module calls AbstractModuleConfig.isDebugLoggingEnabled(); grep for "debug" over the whole module returns nothing. Logging is a plain SLF4J logger at info/warn (OptionsClientEvents only).
- No TODO/FIXME comments anywhere in the module. The repo has no unit tests.
